To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft SPA Update & Disclosure Letter

Here is my analysis of where the Seller's package departs from our agreed positions, with reasoning and recommendations. I've worked through each clause against our playbook.

---

## 1. General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Our position:** Open at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 figure is a *conditional fallback* that may only be used with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft — and none has been given.**

**Reasoning:** The Seller has anchored precisely at our unauthorised fallback. Accepting it now would skip our opening position entirely and deploy a fallback we are not cleared to use. Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do **not** let the drafting drift to 4.8m without explicit written sign-off from Amelia Frost.

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — PUSH BACK (materially off)

**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the **excess** above the basket recoverable.
**Our position:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.

**Reasoning:** Three separate departures, all adverse:
- de minimis 5x too high;
- basket 5x too high;
- "excess above basket" is a *deductible/tipping* mechanic — we want a **first-dollar/tipping-basket** (full recovery once threshold crossed). This single word materially cuts recovery.

Counter to 5k / 50k, first-dollar.

## 3. Time Limits (Clause 12.3/13) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** 18 months for general claims; and a sweeper that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Our position:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (**none given**).

**Reasoning:** Again the Seller anchors on our unauthorised fallback. Counter at 24 months. Separately, the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweeper is a **hidden general-regime override** — it is drafted to pull Fundamental/Title/Tax/fraud into the short general limitation. Reject; insist limitations apply only to general warranty claims, with carve-outs expressly preserved (see below).

## 4. Fundamental / Title Regime (Seller "administrative simplicity") — REJECT

**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties.
**Our position:** separate regime — 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** This collapses our core protection. Title/capacity go to whether we are buying what we think we are buying; a 20% cap / 18-month limit on those is unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to surrender the fundamental regime. Insist on separate treatment: 100% cap, ≥6 years, carved out of basket/de minimis/knowledge.

## 5. Limitations / Exclusive Remedy / Non-Reliance "apply to all Claims" (9.3/12.8/20.5) — REJECT as drafted

**Seller:** these provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
**Our position:** **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.**

**Reasoning:** "All Claims of any nature" would, on its face, cap and time-bar even fraud and apply non-reliance to it. This is a non-negotiable. Insert an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding every limitation, basket, time bar, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. Also ensure Fundamental/Title/Tax/indemnity claims are expressly excluded from the sweeper.

## 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) — REJECT deemed/blanket disclosure

**Seller:** general disclosure of the **entire data room** (DD-002–012) plus Accounts, statutory registers and **publicly searchable records**.
**Our position:** require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Reasoning:** §1.1 "discloses every fact… contained or referred to in the data room" and §1.2 (registers + public records) are exactly the blanket/deemed disclosure we reject. This shifts discovery risk onto us for anything buried anywhere in the data room or a public search. Require that only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter (with sufficient detail to assess nature/scope/impact) qualify. Note §1.4's "nothing admits anything" reservation is standard but combined with blanket disclosure it is one-sided — tie disclosure to fair-disclosure standard.

## 7. Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3) — REJECT

**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
**Our position:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Reasoning:** This is a constructive/imputed-knowledge bar ("discoverable") — far worse than actual knowledge and effectively re-imports deemed disclosure through the back door. Delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, limit to the **actual knowledge of named individuals** and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident).

## 8. Bluefen Consent (Clause 3/6.3) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as **satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) satisfied** as at letter date.
**Our position:** require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer consent.

**Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — plainly material. "Consent-on-delivery" ignores clause 11.3 conditions; a delivered consent subject to unsatisfied conditions is worthless. Make effective Bluefen consent **with evidence of satisfied conditions** a hard Condition Precedent to Completion. Reject reasonable-endeavours-only.

## 9. Riverlark Facility (Clause 2/7) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** release "to be provided **following** Completion"; ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; Disclosure §3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge**.
**Our position:** require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**; a post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval**.

**Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, Riverlark debt and security must be cleared **at** Completion via the funds flow, not left as a post-Completion promise (which leaves the shares/assets encumbered after we own them). Require current payout, direct repayment from completion funds, and discharge of security at Completion. Any post-Completion mechanism needs an irrevocable undertaking from the financier **and** Amelia Frost's approval — not yet sought.

## 10. Employee Bonuses (Funds Flow / Disclosure §5) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in the funds flow. Disclosure confirms on-costs (payroll tax/super) are not addressed.
**Our position:** the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must **not silently exclude** them.

**Reasoning:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities. If they are the Seller's responsibility, that must be documented as a specific funds-flow line item or seller funding — not left silently out, which risks the company (now ours) carrying them. Insist on explicit treatment of the 420k **and** on-costs (super/payroll tax), with a warranty/indemnity that no further employee Completion bonuses exist.

## 11. Ironquay IP Indemnity (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure §4) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate."
**Our position:** **broaden** the narrow indemnity while **preserving the SOW3 cure**; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

**Reasoning:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee, and there is **no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment** in the data room. Our exposure is loss of IP/materials, not just the 180k line item. Broaden the indemnity to cover the consequences of non-transfer/defective assignment of SOW3 materials, while retaining the ability to cure by payment. Do not accept the 180k figure as settled — it is unverified.

## 12. Export/Privacy Incident DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure §6) — PROCESS, not concession

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
**Our position:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.**

**Reasoning:** Correctly, neither side should assert a confirmed breach or a loss figure — the disclosure itself says scope, access and notification status are unresolved (~1,240 records). Don't accept "not material" as a conclusion, but equally don't assert harm. Require: preservation of logs, a completed investigation, ongoing updates/cooperation obligations, and a **specific indemnity** for the incident carved out of the general caps/basket/knowledge bar (so it survives regardless of the general regime outcome). Keep it factual.

## 13. Sandbar Supplier Renewals (Disclosure §8) — ASSESS, don't accept framing

**Seller:** three renewals AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
**Our position:** **assess**; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Reasoning:** Disclosure admits it is silent on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should neither accept "ordinary course" nor assert they are Debt/a price deduction. Request the underlying contracts to assess terminability/accrual, then decide. Keep position open.

## 14. Title (Clause / Disclosure §10) — PUSH BACK

**Seller:** title evidenced by the **DD-012 share register**.
**Our position:** require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.**

**Reasoning:** The company's own register, supplied by the Seller, is not independent verification of title — and §10 expressly admits we have not completed our own verification. Require independent evidence of ownership/encumbrances/authority, backed by a 100%-cap fundamental title warranty (per item 4), carved out of the general regime and knowledge bar.

## 15. Tax / IP — KEEP OPEN

**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
**Our position:** Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

**Reasoning:** The Seller is trying to fold Tax and IP into the (deficient) general regime — another hidden override. These are **not settled**. Reserve our position; keep them as separate categories and do not let the general cap/time-limit/basket silently govern them.

## 16. Structural point — Hidden General-Regime Override

Across clauses 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5, the Fundamental/Title "simplicity" proposal, and the Tax/IP line, the Seller is systematically trying to make **one general regime govern everything**. Our playbook requires Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept **separate with no hidden override**. Insist on clear ring-fencing of each regime.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our counter |
|---|-------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m**; 4.8m needs Amelia Frost written authority (none given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar** |
| 3 | Time limit | 18m + "all Claims" sweeper | **24m**; delete sweeper; 18m needs Frost approval (none) |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | same as general | **Separate: 100% cap, ≥6yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Limitations/non-reliance "all Claims" | applies to everything | **Carve out fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from all limits — unwaivable**; exclude Title/Tax/indemnities |
| 6 | Disclosure | whole data room + public registers | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | actual + "discoverable" | **Delete**; if any, actual knowledge of named persons; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen | reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied as CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | release post-Completion | **Payout + direct repayment at Completion + security discharge**; post-Completion needs irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval |
| 10 | Bonuses (420k) | off funds flow, "Seller's matter" | **Specific line item / seller-funded, incl. on-costs** |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3-only indemnity | **Broaden (preserve SOW3 cure)**; 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "not material" | **Preserve/investigate/update + specific indemnity carved out**; assert no harm, no breach |
| 13 | Sandbar 330k | "ordinary course" | **Assess underlying contracts; no auto-Debt/deduction** |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence** |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "settled" | **Keep OPEN; no unlimited liability; no hidden override** |
| 16 | Structure | one general regime for all | **Ring-fence categories; no hidden override** |

**Three hard lines to flag to the deal principals:**
1. **Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out** — must override every cap, basket, time bar, exclusive remedy and non-reliance; unwaivable. The "all Claims of any nature" drafting currently defeats this.
2. **Fundamental/Title regime** must stay separate (100% / ≥6yrs) — reject the "administrative simplicity" merger.
3. **Authority gates:** the Seller has anchored on both of our unauthorised fallbacks (20% cap and 18-month limit). Neither can be accepted without **Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the draft** — which has not been given. Open at 25% / 24 months.

I have **not** sent anything externally or taken any action — this is internal advice only. Want me to draft the mark-up / issues list for the Seller, or a short note to Amelia Frost on the two authority points?
